title: Similar and Congruent Triangles
seo_title: Grade 9 Similar and Congruent Triangles Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Through investigation, establish the minimum conditions for congruent triangles; through investigation, establish the minimum conditions for similar triangles; solve geometric problems involving unknown sides and angles in triangles, using known properties of triangles, as well as definitions of congruence and similarity.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 9 worksheets: angles in triangles, congruent triangles, similar triangles and scale factors. 100 questions with memos.
key_sub: Similar: equal angles, sides in proportion.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Congruent triangles are identical: SSS, SAS, AAS or RHS.
  • Similar triangles have equal angles and sides in proportion.
  • Match corresponding sides by the equal angles.
  • Scale factor = a side of one triangle ÷ the matching side of the other.

Examples

Example

Similar triangles: 6 ↔ 9, 8 ↔ ?

scale factor 1,5

Answer: 12

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
AAA for congruenceEqual angles prove similarity only.
Wrong sidesMatch sides opposite equal angles.
Adding the factorMultiply.

items.q: An exterior angle of a triangle is 111°. One of the opposite interior angles is 70°. Find the other opposite interior angle.
items.e: Exterior angle = sum of the two opposite interior angles: 111 − 70 = 41°.

items.q: A triangle has interior angles of 56° and 66°. The side next to the third angle is extended. What is the exterior angle there?
items.e: The exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles: 56 + 66 = 122°. (Or 180 − third angle 58°.)

items.q: A triangle has interior angles of 68° and 69°. The side next to the third angle is extended. What is the exterior angle there?
items.e: The exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles: 68 + 69 = 137°. (Or 180 − third angle 43°.)

items.q: A triangle has interior angles of 46° and 65°. The side next to the third angle is extended. What is the exterior angle there?

items.q: A triangle has interior angles of 76° and 68°. The side next to the third angle is extended. What is the exterior angle there?

items.q: A triangle has angles 50°, 60° and 70°. What type of triangle is it?
items.e: All angles are less than 90° and all different: acute-angled scalene.

items.q: Two triangles each have sides 6 cm and 8 cm with a 50° angle between them. Are they congruent?
items.e: Two sides and the included angle: SAS.

items.q: Two triangles are congruent. Which condition is this? Two angles and a side that is not between them are equal (AAS).
items.e: This is ASA.

items.q: Two triangles are congruent. Which condition is this? All three sides of one triangle are equal to all three sides of the other.
items.e: This is SSS.

items.q: Two right-angled triangles both have a hypotenuse of 13 cm and a side of 5 cm. Are they congruent?
c: Only if they face the same way
items.e: Right angle, hypotenuse, side: RHS.

items.q: Both triangles have angles 40°, 60° and 80°. Are they definitely congruent?
c: No, because the angles are different
No — they are similar, but could be different sizes
items.e: Equal angles only prove the triangles are the same shape: similar, not necessarily congruent.

items.q: A shape is reflected. Is the image congruent to the original?
c: Only if the mirror line is vertical
items.e: Reflection keeps all lengths and angles, so yes.

items.q: Two triangles are congruent. Which condition is this? Two sides and the angle between them are equal.
items.e: This is SAS.

items.q: Two triangles are congruent. Which condition is this? Two angles and the side between them are equal.
items.e: This is ASA.

items.q: Triangle 1 has sides 5, 7, 9 cm. Triangle 2 has sides 9, 5, 7 cm. Are they congruent?
c: No, the sides are in a different order
items.e: The same three side lengths in any order: yes, by SSS.

items.q: Two triangles are congruent. Which condition is this? Both have a right angle, equal hypotenuses and one other equal side.
items.e: This is RHS.

items.q: Which of these does NOT prove two triangles are congruent?
items.e: Three equal angles only show the triangles are similar: AAA.
